title: fix(layout): the mobile tab bar opens the page its sidebar row opens, every tab href from resolveHref (objectui#11211)
body:
Fixes #11211
Clause-②: no

## What changed

`AppSchemaRenderer`'s mobile tab bar (`mobileNavMode: 'bottom_nav'`, the `MobileBottomNav` function) built each tab's href itself, one branch per entry type. Those branches are deleted. Each tab now uses the same rule pair as the sidebar, called with the same arguments that the sidebar's `NavigationRenderer` gets inside `AppSchemaRenderer`:

- **The page a tab opens** comes from `resolveHref(item, basePath)`. This is the ruled change.
- **Whether a tab is highlighted** comes from `resolveActiveNavItem(items, pathname, search, basePath)`, the inverse of `resolveHref`. It elects over the whole tree, as the sidebar does. This is an in-place fix (see below).
- **Which window an `external` answer opens in:** the tab is a plain anchor with `target="_blank"` and `rel="noopener noreferrer"`, which is how the sidebar draws it. Also an in-place fix (see below).

No prop, export, type or accepted value changes. `resolveHref` itself is not touched.

## Measured before the change (the dispatch's Zone 2)

**1. Red reproduced on `origin/main` (`2124d04111`).** I ran the new pin against the unchanged renderer. The four card rows went red with the card's own "tab href" values, and the control stayed green (`Tests 6 failed | 1 passed (7)`; the two other reds are the active-state pin and the external pin).

| entry | tab href at `2124d04111` | `resolveHref` = the sidebar's link |
|:--|:--|:--|
| plain `object` (control) | `/apps/crm/account` | `/apps/crm/account` |
| `recordId: 'u1'` | `/apps/crm/sys_user` | `/apps/crm/sys_user/record/u1` |
| `filters: { status: 'open' }` | `/apps/crm/task` | `/apps/crm/task/data?filter%5Bstatus%5D=open` |
| `runAction: 'task_create'` | `/apps/crm/task` | `/apps/crm/task?runAction=task_create` |
| `metadata:resource` with `params: { type: 'object' }` | `/apps/crm/component/metadata/resource?type=object` | `/apps/crm/metadata/object` |

A scratch probe (deleted, never committed) found three more differences in the same branches. Deleting the branches removes them too: a `page` entry dropped its `params` (`/apps/crm/page/home`, where the sidebar opens `/apps/crm/page/home?tab=x`), `recordMode: 'edit'` was ignored, and `viewName` together with `runAction` lost the action. After the change the same probe showed every tab href equal to `resolveHref`'s answer, except for the out-of-scope `action` entry described in the Acceptance notes.

**2. Template context.** Inside `AppSchemaRenderer`, `InternalSidebar` renders `NavigationRenderer` with `basePath` and no `templateContext`, so the sidebar calls `resolveHref(item, basePath, undefined)`. `AppSchemaRendererProps` has no template context, so the bar passes none either. The arguments are the same and nothing new was added. In the probe, a `recordId: '{current_user_id}'` entry gave `/apps/crm/sys_user` on both surfaces.

**3. Did the old branches handle anything `resolveHref` does not? No.** For `dashboard`, `report`, plain `object`, `viewName`, `url`, a non-metadata `component`, `doc` and `action`, both sides gave the same href, and an entry with a missing target gave `#` on both. The only extra behaviour was on broken input: with no `objectName` the old branch gave `/apps/crm/undefined`, and a `componentRef` made only of colons gave a bare `/component/` route. `resolveHref` handles both better. Groups never needed an href: the bar flattens them before any href is computed, and that part is unchanged.

**4. The `doc` branch**, added by objectui#11197, already called `resolveHref`. That call is now the only path, for every type.

## Two in-place fixes in the same function (the bounded exemption)

Both belong to the card's defect class: the bar was computing something that the `resolveHref` / `resolveActiveNavItem` pair already answers. Both now use the sidebar's own call. They live in the same function and are covered by the same test family, and no other claim holds this file.

- **Highlighted tab (this change requires it).** The old check was `location.pathname.startsWith(href)`. For `filters` and `runAction` entries, `resolveHref` returns an href with a query string, and a pathname can never start with that. So changing the hrefs alone would have left those tabs unhighlighted on their own pages. Ablation C below measured this: on the filtered list, no tab was highlighted (`expected [] to deeply equal [ 'Open Tasks' ]`). The `resolveActiveNavItem` docblock requires every "which menu am I in" surface to use it. Now at most one tab is highlighted, and it is the row the sidebar highlights. At `2124d04111`, on `/apps/crm/task`, the filtered tab and the quick-action tab were both highlighted.
- **External links.** For a `url` entry with `target: '_blank'`, `resolveHref` answers `external: true`. The sidebar opens such a link in a new tab, while the bar opened it in the app's own window. Measured at `2124d04111`: the href matched, but there was no `target` attribute.

## Tests

The new pin is `packages/layout/src/__tests__/AppSchemaRenderer.mobileTabHref-11211.test.tsx`. It covers the four card rows plus the control. Each row asserts that the tab href equals `resolveHref`'s answer and equals the sidebar link for the same entry. Each row also pins `resolveHref`'s answer to the card's table, which shows the row really goes through the branch it names. There is one active-state pin and one external pin.

Ablations were run on the committed fix with `ablation-replace`. In every leg the anchor went from 1 hit to 0 and the file's blob hash changed. The restore was proven for every leg: the blob matched `HEAD` and `git diff HEAD` was empty.

| leg | mutation | red | green |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| A | the old `object` branch put back in front of `resolveHref` | record, filters and runAction rows (tab hrefs exactly as in the card's table) | control, metadata, active, external |
| B | the old `component` branch put back | metadata row (`/apps/crm/component/metadata/resource?type=object`) | the other 6 |
| C | the old pathname-prefix highlight check | active-state pin (`[]`) | the other 6 |
| D | the `external` answer ignored | external pin (`target` is `null`) | the other 6 |

Gates, all run at `6f5ff7bf0a` (this branch's head):

- `pnpm --filter '@object-ui/layout^...' build` (through the verify lock): `VERDICT command-exit 0`. It built types, core, components, react, react-runtime, sdui-parser and data-objectstack.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/layout type-check` (through the verify lock): `VERDICT command-exit 0`. The script name was echoed. `--listFiles` shows both `tsc` passes include their changed file: the main config includes `AppSchemaRenderer.tsx` and `tsconfig.test.json` includes the new pin.
- `pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 packages/layout/` (through the verify lock): `Test Files 32 passed (32)`, `Tests 321 passed (321)`. This includes the objectui#11197 `doc` tab pin and the objectui#9868 tab-label pin, both of which cover this bar.
- App-shell suites: `git grep -l 'AppSchemaRenderer\|mobileNavMode'` finds no suite under `packages/app-shell` or `apps/console` that mounts the renderer. The two app-shell hits are comments.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/layout lint` exit 0 (0 errors). The new pin has no findings. The two warnings in `AppSchemaRenderer.tsx` are in the `AppSchemaRenderer` area-election `useEffect`, which this diff does not touch.
- `pnpm check:new-line-citations` (`VERDICT new-cross-file-line-citations: 0 new citation(s)`), `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs`, `pnpm changeset:check`, `pnpm check:control-bytes`, `node scripts/check-changeset-claims.mjs` and `node scripts/check-changeset-overwrite.mjs` all exited 0.

Changeset: `.changeset/11211-layout-mobile-tab-resolvehref.md`, `@object-ui/layout` `patch`.

## Acceptance notes

These are out of scope here and reported to the seat, not filed by this run:

- **The bar does not apply the sidebar's entry checks.** At both `2124d04111` and `6f5ff7bf0a`, with `checkPermission` returning false for every entry, an entry with `visible: false` and an entry whose `requiredPermissions` are denied still appear as tabs, while the sidebar hides both. An `action` entry appears as a dead link (href `/`), while the sidebar draws a button or hides it. The checks are a different defect class from this card, and the sidebar's guard is not a single pinned call, so it was not fixed here.
- **`mobileNavMode` on the app document is kept and then ignored.** `skills/objectui/guides/mobile.md` says to set `mobileNavMode` "on the app schema that `AppSchemaRenderer` ... renders". Measured: objectui's `AppComponentSchema` parses a document that carries `mobileNavMode: 'bottom_nav'` and keeps the key, but `AppSchemaRenderer` draws no bar from it. Only the prop (the node input) turns the bar on. `skills/**` is a governed surface, so any change there needs its own PR.
